solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maintain wild stares

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters of the next word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up a fierce, staring glare.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to state it firmly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Petitions about cricket club initially slow prosperity

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: to petition a court is to sue, so petitions = sues

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word slow

explanation.surface: Legal claims around a cricket club are holding back its fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Success and prosperity are synonyms for doing well or thriving.

clue.text: Have a meal in German city

definitions.meaning: the German verb meaning to eat
a large industrial city in the Ruhr

explanation.surface: Someone dines out somewhere in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a foreign-language one: the German word for 'eat' is also the name of a city in the Ruhr.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr city shares its name with the German infinitive meaning to eat.

clue.text: The copy about slippery eels is missing set subject

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the copy goes round the jumbled eels

parts.note: MS, manuscript, is the printer's term for copy to be set

indicators.note: slippery eels wriggle out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer's draft about slippery eels lacks any real subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery' turns EELS into ELES, which MS goes 'about' to make MELESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece with no set topic or unifying motif lacks a theme.

clue.text: Neutral state of high energy on steamer

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a steamer

explanation.surface: A dull, neutral condition found aboard a high-powered steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like part of a physics phrase, but it signals ENERGY rearranged into GREYNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grey is the neutral colour between black and white, so the quality of being grey is a neutral state.

clue.text: Painted brilliantly, which is also commented on

definitions.meaning: given a shiny coat of high-sheen paint
provided with an explanatory note or gloss on a text

explanation.surface: A text was given a shiny finish and also annotated.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is coated with shiny paint; the other is annotated with marginal explanations.

clue.text: Try French art for example

parts.note: in French tu es means thou art
say is used like 'for example', introducing an instance

explanation.surface: An invitation to have a go at French art, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old second-person form of 'are', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To essay something is to attempt it, a formal synonym of try.

clue.text: What one is worth when placed in difficulties

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces sit inside the other

parts.note: nets are traps, so difficulties one is caught in
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
set means placed, as in set down

explanation.surface: A sobering thought about one's value when in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Net worth is the balance of holdings after liabilities are deducted.

clue.text: Female forecaster always in short session

indicators.note: in puts the poetic word inside the abbreviated one

parts.note: sess. is the abbreviation of session
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

explanation.surface: A woman predicting the future is always in a brief sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A female prophet or soothsayer foretells the future.

clue.text: Disturbing sound in tape unit for French ballet

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a cassette is a unit holding recording tape
noise is unwanted, disturbing sound

explanation.surface: An annoying hiss on a tape spoils a recording of a French ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French title of Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker ballet.

clue.text: Despicable behaviour showing girl's in confusion

indicators.note: in puts the girl's name inside the disorder

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion
Anne's, a girl's name with possessive

explanation.surface: A girl's poor conduct shows she is muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanness is unkind, low-minded or contemptible conduct.

clue.text: Affirmative answers being found in heart of Harley Street

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside another
heart points to the centre, the two middle letters of the two-word street name

parts.note: esse is Latin for being or existence

explanation.surface: Positive replies are found at the heart of London's medical quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: Harley Street is the London street famous for private doctors; its middle letters are Y and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'yes' repeatedly gives affirmative replies; the plural form names them.

clue.text: Take for granted bird's sex appeal is returning

indicators.note: returning means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: emu's, of the flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: Assume a bird's allure is coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: To presuppose something without proof is a direct synonym.

clue.text: International organisation's fidelity to audience is loosened

parts.note: UN is the United Nations

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard, so a word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: fidelity is trust or loyalty

explanation.surface: A global body's loyalty to the public weakens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trust' said aloud sounds like 'trussed', meaning tied up; adding UN reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied or unbound, with the bindings released, is to be loosened.

clue.text: Aristocrat beginning to eat potato dish

parts.note: a duchess is a noblewoman

indicators.note: beginning to takes only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A noblewoman starts to tuck into a plate of potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Duchesse potatoes are mashed with egg, piped and baked.

clue.text: Angry soldier eating one's roll

indicators.note: eating says one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: cross means angry
I is the Roman numeral one
a soldier ant is a worker ant, so ant = soldier

explanation.surface: An irate soldier is munching his breakfast bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent-shaped French pastry is a type of bread roll.

clue.text: Predatory insect's advanced in part of log

parts.note: mantis's, of the praying mantis, a predatory insect
A stands for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: A predatory insect has made progress through part of a fallen log.
explanation.definitionFit: In logarithms the fractional decimal part following the characteristic is called this.

clue.text: Soften cooked sausage

indicators.note: cooked suggests something altered or fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to make a sausage tender.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease or mollify pain or anger is to soften it.

clue.text: Stewardess with close shave?

definitions.meaning: a young woman working in the air, read whimsically

explanation.surface: A flight attendant has a narrow escape.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss in flight; whimsically, also a single woman in the air.

clue.text: Versatile son is a legendary Gaelic poet

indicators.note: versatile means adaptable, able to take other forms, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A talented son turns out to be a poet of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the bard of Gaelic legend whose poems James Macpherson claimed to translate.

clue.text: Kill with spear because age is deforming

parts.note: as means because, as in 'as it rained'

indicators.note: deforming means bending out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A violent death by spear blamed on the warping effects of age.
explanation.definitionFit: The light Zulu throwing-spear can also be used as a verb for spearing someone.

clue.text: Southern capitals getting covered in dust? Exactly

indicators.note: getting covered in says the first pieces go inside the dust

parts.note: ash is a fine dusty residue
UC means upper case, capital letters

explanation.surface: Cities in the south are coated in dust.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the precise sense, strictly speaking, exactly.

clue.text: Famous writer — he's grabbing female's end

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: taken as written
-ess is the suffix that ends female forms such as actress

explanation.surface: A writer is caught clutching a woman's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is Hermann Hesse, author of Steppenwolf; 'end' means a suffix, not a last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann, the Nobel-winning German novelist, is a celebrated author.

clue.text: African prince has mixed cases for fish

parts.note: Ras is an Ethiopian title for a prince or ruler

indicators.note: mixed means stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An African royal has jumbled boxes of seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: The scorpion fish used in bouillabaisse goes by this French name.

clue.text: Famous writer's improper

definitions.meaning: belonging to Kingsley or Martin Amis, both novelists, written with a possessive s

explanation.surface: A noted author's behaviour is out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wrong or out of place is improper.

clue.text: Killing donkey is against new orders

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: orders as a verb, arranging, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A donkey resists fresh commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orders' is a verb (puts in order), signalling an anagram of IS AGAINST plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: Murdering a prominent figure is a form of killing.

clue.text: Rocks start to seem unnecessary

parts.note: the Needles are chalk rocks off the Isle of Wight

indicators.note: start to takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Rocks begin to look pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are a famous row of chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncalled for or superfluous is unnecessary.

clue.text: Cough needs fresh tissues with no end of resistance

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made over in a new order
with no says a letter is left out of the pool
end of picks the final letter of resistance

explanation.surface: A cough calls for new tissues when resistance runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: TISSUES without E (the end of 'resistance') leaves TISSUS, which 'fresh' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussis is the medical Latin term for a cough.
